correctness.rationale: The normalized analytic outer q-th root G has H² norm one since qp=2 and inner multiplication preserves boundary modulus. Writing x=|G(0)|>0, Parseval gives |G'(0)|≤sqrt(1-x²). Schwarz–Pick and the product rule then give the objective (1-rho²+q rho t)/(1+t²)^(q/2) for t=sqrt(x^(-2)-1). The sign of its derivative is the sign of rho-(1-rho²)t-(q-1)rho t². For rho>0 it changes once, at the claimed root in (0,1/sqrt(q-1)]; for rho=0 the unique maximum is at zero. For 0<rho<1 equality requires a disk automorphism for I, a linear polynomial for G, and matched phases in their derivative terms; the displayed factors have exactly those phases, the linear factor is outer because t<1, and the norm is one. The endpoint equalities reduce to the Schwarz lemma and constant G at rho=0, and constant I and the linear G at rho=1. The stationarity polynomial evaluated at 2 rho/q is -rho(q-2)(q-2rho²)/q², so the envelope derivative (q t-2rho)/(1+t²)^(q/2) is positive for rho>0. Implicit analyticity and oddness of t at zero give t=rho+O(rho³), yielding the claimed quadratic expansion; evaluating the envelope derivative at one gives the other expansion. If f(a)=0, I=B_a J gives rho≤|a|, and strict increase forces constant J in equality when a≠0. Its phase parameter is eta=-|a|/a; at a=0 equality means a multiple of z by a unit scalar.
residual_risks: The finite verifier samples the algebra and asymptotics only; it does not certify any infinite parameter domain. The proof covers the entire inner factor, including the possibility of a singular inner factor before equality is imposed.

evidence: Set s_*=(1-p/2)^(1/p). The old transition satisfies s_p<s_*sqrt(p/(2-p))<s_*. Its frontier reaches its global maximum uniquely at s_*, and for s≥s_* the unique optimizer up to rotations is (1+beta z)^q/(1+beta²)^(q/2), where s=(1+beta²)^(-q/2). These optimizers are outer.

The separate unrestricted first-coefficient constant is already known (Brevig–Saksman); qualitative outerness for bounded linear extremizers (Brevig–Søvik) is not itself the decisive quantitative prior coverage.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For any A,B≥0 not both zero, the support objective A s+B Phi_1(p,s) is maximized at s≥s_*, since both terms there at s_* dominate those at every s<s_*. Thus the only part of the known frontier needed for all these linear combinations is its outer branch, which remains sharp under a restriction to outer factors.

evidence: For the conditional problem write f=IF and apply the known Phi_1(p,s) to F, where s=|F(0)|. By Schwarz–Pick, |f'(0)|≤(1-rho²)s+rho Phi_1(p,s). Below s_* this cannot maximize; above s_* the known sharp outer optimizer has parameter beta in [0,1/sqrt(q-1)]. Substitution gives (1-rho²+q rho beta)/(1+beta²)^(q/2); its derivative gives the frozen stationary quadratic.

The known frontier optimizers attain the bound with the corresponding Schwarz–Pick automorphism and aligned phases, and its uniqueness on s≥s_* fixes the outer equality factor. For prescribed zeros use the same support calculation with the quotient g; its optimizer is already outer and hence gives exactly the single-Blaschke equality case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Unlike applying the old theorem to f itself, applying it to the appropriate factor gives the entire sharp profile. The endpoints are the norm of evaluation and the classical unrestricted derivative extremum. The monotonicity witness and endpoint expansions follow by differentiating and expanding the explicit one-variable maximum; they require no further extremal theorem.

For a prescribed zero, f=B_a g is a norm-preserving correspondence with unrestricted g. The derivative at zero is the linear functional B_a'(0)g(0)+B_a(0)g'(0). The magnitudes of its weights are 1-|a|² and |a|.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The prescribed-zero bound is the support value of the known first-jet body at those nonnegative weights, with phase alignment obtainable by constants and rotations. A naive substitution of |f(0)|≤|a| in the old theorem, without dividing by B_a, gives a different and loose bound; that is not the relevant implication.

originality.rationale: The frozen problem conditions on a different quantity than Brevig–Grepstad–Instanes, but the proper comparison applies their stronger exact fixed-origin first-coefficient frontier to the outer factor (or, for a prescribed zero, to the quotient by its Blaschke factor), not to the original f. Their Theorem 12 and Corollary 13 then give the sharp formula and equality cases by elementary support maximization. Strict increase and the stated endpoint expansions are elementary calculus consequences of that same formula. There is no verified claim of an earlier statement worded with the same parameter; this is verified implication, not a title match.
residual_risks: No absolute claim about historical priority is made; older mixed functional or interpolation work may cover further cases. The originality failure is based on a verified implication of the accessible Theorem 12, not on the inaccessible thesis.

value.rationale: Prescribing a zero is a natural problem, and the record gives a concise, correct direct proof. But the quantified loss and exact extremizers come from the known first-jet frontier by norm-preserving division or inner–outer factorization, phase alignment, and a single scalar optimization. The additional monotonicity and endpoint coefficients are routine calculus of the resulting formula; no independently useful exact result not mechanically implied by the prior frontier survives as stated.
residual_risks: This assessment concerns the frozen invariant, not higher-order jets, multi-zero constraints, or quantitative distance to extremizers, which the record does not claim.
